newsitem.title: USA: Pinkerton says McBride stay reinstated.
newsitem.headline: Pinkerton says McBride stay reinstated.

text.p: Security firm Pinkerton's Inc said a Michigan appeals court granted its request to reinstate a stay of execution of the judgment in the Sean McBride case.
McBride was shot in January 1994 by a man who was making comments about his homosexuality. It happened by a building where an unarmed Pinkerton security officer was stationed.
In November, Pinkerton announced plans to appeal a $10 million judgment by a Michigan jury.
It said it acted appropriately and could not have prevented the incident from occuring.
Execution of the judgment was stayed by the Wayne County circuit court pending Pinkerton's appeal, but the trial court lifted the stay on Friday, the company said.
Then, the trial court issued an order reversing its decision of Friday and nullifying any alleged attempts by the plaintiff's counsel to take advantage of the stay's brief lifting, the company said.
"Pinkerton remains confident that it will prevail on its appeal of the case," C. Michael Carter, Pinkerton executive vice president and general counsel, said.
The company was not immediately available to comment further.
